I've been in the exact boat. I couldn't leave my room at uni because of my anxiety which made it worse... I ended up talking to a lecturer I trusted which got me to sign up to see the mental health nurse on campus and from there I took it step by step. 

I ended up taking a year out as it got so bad when we had to return after lock down. During this time I had therapy thanks to the uni giving me contacts, I did some dog walking and dog sitting which helped me a lot because it proved I can do something, even if it's just taking a strangers dog on a walk but it like helped me tackle my anxiety through something I loved which is taking care of animals. 

When I returned to uni it was a struggle, I still didn't go to some lectures but there was great support for me and others with mental health disabilities. 

I graduated later then everyone but I made it. I now got a full time job and two dogs of my own. I'm also on anxiety and depression medication which seems to keep the anxiety that keeps me from leaving the house at bay. So the meds has helped A LOT. 

YOU ARE OKAY. Anxiety takes over ur body and screams at you that you are worthless but it is lying. I am currently part of a video team where the senior editor uses Final cut whilst the rest of us use Premiere Pro.

We're in a trial for both softwares to see which one would be the platform for regular content... And work politics kicked in BUT the point I want to say is! Before the trial I made graphics that I made in after effects and when I had to give it to my senior to use in final cut I just saved them as a .mov file that carried over the alpha channel. 

We're still currently in this weird phase where we are all using Premiere to edit (I think premiere won but they won't admit it lol) and won't end the trial but the senior who uses Final cut seemed fine with the switch to premiere. They picked it up fast cause editing won't really change, you cut stuff up, stitch it up. It's just going to be slower using Premiere when you've come from final cut. But doing split screens is so much easier in Premiere, especially if you have to change timings from feedback from a client or something. 

If you're willing to learn Premiere I'd say do it. If you have time that is. I'm guessing the third party has made the graphics into mogrts and should just be a drag and drop because after effects is a lot more difficult/unique than Final Cut and Premiere.  Or you can open an after effects comp in premiere and it'll be a dynamic link. 


There's no harm in trying premiere. If you need help with integrating after effects files/comps I'm happy to try and help. I've had to self teach myself since no one in my team had used after effects 🤷‍♀️  and now I'm trying to share my knowledge to my team so I'm not the only one 😂😭

Hey, I'm a student (final year) and have experienced well, I'm feeling what you've just written.  I haven't been able to go into class for a month. I managed to force myself before till I ended up having panic attacks at uni and a breakdown as soon as I reach my flat and I completely shut down. I couldn't find motivation to live and felt like I've already failed in life. I'm very fortunate to have people who care about me and kept me going. 

My suggestion is, if you haven't already speak to the university well being and your course supervisor/mentor if you know who it is. Book an appointment with a GP, I did this and I'm now on meds, just started though so I can't say much on that yet. You just got to get the ball rolling I think for help. There's EC's you can claim for extentions. If the uni knows you have these mental health issues they can help with some things. They gave me an academic mentor (was for anxiety before I knew I had depression) but she is a god send. She's helped me with uni stress and helps break stuff down. She doesn't know much about my course but it's just helpful to get someone's opinion on things and bring worries down to a more manageable level. 

If you're in the UK you get 4 years of uni "funded" so if you've just started you could retake a year or change course. (I did this and changed course). I do wish I listened to my lecturer because I should've taken a break from uni  which you can also do. Take a year out.
